summary.headline: NTPC standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR 45,752 crore and PAT 14% to INR 5,320 crore; NGEL revenue up 53%.
summary.overview: NTPC posted strong Q2 FY27 standalone growth, with revenue from operations up 17% YoY to INR 45,752 crore and PAT up 14% to INR 5,320 crore, helped by O&M gains and lower fixed-cost disincentives. Group PAT for H1 rose 26% to INR 14,247 crore. NGEL's revenue and EBITDA grew about 53-57% in Q2, but renewable capacity addition is behind plan due to transmission delays, with FY27 group target cut from about 9.5 GW to about 8 GW. Management flagged coal supply tightness (5.2 MMT stock, about 7 days) and is sourcing 13 MMT from alternative sources for H2. A first interim dividend of INR 3 per share was recommended.

segments.name: NTPC standalone (conventional)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 45,752 crore and PAT INR 5,320 crore; other income fell INR 432 crore on lower dividends from subsidiaries/JVs (down INR 481 crore) and LPS down 28%. Coal fixed-cost disincentive fell to INR 332 crore from INR 625 crore a year ago.

segments.name: NTPC Group generation and coal
segments.commentary: H1 group generation 236 BU vs 214 BU (+10.4%); NTPC coal stations PLF 75.11% vs rest-of-India 68.35%. Captive coal dispatch 26.13 MMT vs 21.63 MMT (+21%).

segments.name: NTPC Green Energy (NGEL)
segments.commentary: H1 generation 10.88 BU vs 6.76 BU (+60%); Q2 revenue INR 938.16 crore and EBITDA INR 829.69 crore (about 88% margin). Curtailment from transmission constraints is ongoing.

segments.name: NVVN (trading)
segments.commentary: H1 power traded 31 BU vs 24.8 BU (+25%); commissioned 250 MW / 500 MWh BESS as an implementing agency.

segments.name: THDC and BRBCL
segments.commentary: THDC profit up on 500 MW PSP and 660 MW Khurja (full-year effect this year); INR 221 crore uplift cited. BRBCL Q2 profit up INR 64 crore on lower finance cost after refinancing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group capacity addition revised to about 8 GW from earlier 9.5 GW, all renewable; NGEL on-ground capacity expected about 6.35 GW by year-end, with a 1.5 GW shortfall attributed to transmission.
FY28 target about 9.6 GW for the group (thermal 1,460 MW, hydro 444 MW, renewable 7,735 MW); FY29 target about 10.9 GW (thermal 3,070 MW, renewable 7,807 MW).
Transmission constraints for NGEL expected to be resolved by mid-July 2027.
Group capacity under construction: 37 GW, including 17.32 GW coal, about 3.6 GW hydro and about 16 GW renewables.
Plan to tender about 4.8 GW of new thermal in Q1-Q2 FY28 with estimated capex INR 67,000 crore; pithead and non-pithead split equally.
Sinnar turnaround targeted by December 2026 or January 2027.
Battery storage: about 1,350 MW of NGEL BESS expected by mid-FY27; full-scale BESS largely in FY29; contractor issues being addressed, with BESS targeted by April.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 group capex INR 23,932 crore (vs INR 23,115 crore); standalone capex INR 14,398 crore (vs INR 14,149 crore).
Group gross PP&E INR 4,85,444 crore at 30 Sep 2026, up 11% YoY. Installed group capacity 91,506 MW; H1 additions 2,398 MW (NGEL 1,136 MW).
Lara Stage 3 (1,600 MW) awarded and limited notice to proceed issued pending environmental clearance.
Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 approved 30 Sep 2026: outlay INR 1,86,405 crore, central support INR 54,082 crore, targeted for FY32-33.
Storage plan: about 47 GWh overall, of which 5 GWh at thermal co-location; NGEL targeting about 41-42 GWh, with 40 GWh tender via ICB for direct Chinese procurement.
Pumped storage: first DPR (Maharashtra) due December, Amba DPR by March; award after DPR and TEC.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 15% and generation about 11% in H1 FY27; October demand up 21%. Peak demand met 271 GW.
Coal PLF across India rose to 70.37% in H1 FY27 from 66.02%; CIL and SCCL supply constrained, stocks critical.
Ratnagiri gas plant running on imported LNG at $16-32/MMBtu, average below $28-29; fuel cost about INR 26/kWh.
Ratnagiri profit growth driven by generation in a demand-led market, sold via market operations as PPA issues persist.
Regulatory deferral: INR 862 crore reversal of excess depreciation for Bongaigaon, nil PAT impact.
Curtailment: NGEL losses partly shifted via PPA extensions; T-GNA revenue covers O&M and interest but not depreciation. Revenue loss not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is government pushing for more thermal capacity, and what new thermal is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to tender about 4.8 GW of thermal in Q1-Q2 FY28 (Jhabua 2, Talcher 4, Talcher Kaniha 3, Bhilai, BRBCL 2), with 3-4 GW more under feasibility study.

qa_highlights.question: Is NGEL's curtailment easing and how much revenue was lost?
qa_highlights.answer: Connectivity constraints expected to clear by mid-July 2027; revenue loss not quantified, with lost generation shifted into extended PPA terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the RE addition target be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Original NGEL estimate was about 8 GW; now expected about 6.5 GW built, with about 1.5 GW held up by transmission and carried into next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated PAT grow faster than regulated equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited O&M gains and operational efficiency; expects profit growth to keep significantly exceeding regulated equity growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the C&I strategy and is thermal included?
qa_highlights.answer: An EOI for C&I partners covering power and heat closes end-November 2026, open to renewable, hydro or thermal supply.

qa_highlights.question: Why does BESS take 12-18 months and is there a merchant plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Utility-scale batteries and DC/AC integration need the time; management is replacing underperforming contractors and targets BESS commissioning by April 2027. No merchant BESS was confirmed.

risks_watch: Transmission delays in Khavda and other RE corridors continue to hold back NGEL CODs; connectivity expected by mid-July 2027.
Coal supply: 5.2 MMT stock (about 7 days); 13 MMT tender for H2 FY27 and 4 MMT additional domestic coal award pending.
Renewable target slippage: FY27 group target cut from about 9.5 GW to about 8 GW.
Other income under pressure from lower dividends from subsidiaries and JVs (down INR 481 crore) and lower LPS.
BESS execution depends on contractor performance and the upcoming 40 GWh ICB tender.
Pumped storage: DPRs due December 2026 and March 2027 before awards.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, operating performance and profit growth, but cautious and somewhat hedged on renewable capacity and transmission timelines, with several answers deferred to later data.
key_quotes: Rising demand during both peak and non-peak hours creates growth opportunities.
So, more specific to NGEL, our transmission constraint or the connectivity issue which we are facing will all be surmounted by next year, mid-July.
Profit is a different thing than a dividend payout. So, profitability has come out of better efficiency.
